# COLLISIONS.md - build-fingerprint collisions

Generated by `scripts/make_collisions.py` from the rows in `data/` (5828 rows).

The research tooling uses `zval_ptr_dtor mod 0x1000` - the low 12 bits of the ELF st_value, the bits that survive ASLR in a leaked pointer - as a build fingerprint. A collision means the fingerprint alone cannot tell the two builds apart. Pairs only form within one architecture (`meta.arch`): an offset is usable only against a target of the same ELF machine, so x86_64 and aarch64 rows never pair even when their low 12 bits coincide. Verdicts:

- **identical** - the full st_value matches too: the two builds are interchangeable for that symbol (same offset, same layout).
- **mod-only** - only the low 12 bits match; the full offsets differ, so any other known offset still distinguishes the builds.
